name: Bhida Par Eeda
subtitle: okra fried dry with onion and eggs cracked over the top

ingredients.qty: 400g, wiped dry and cut into 2cm rounds

prepNotes: Wash the okra a good hour ahead and dry every pod with a cloth. Any water left on them turns the dish slimy.
Use a knife and board that are completely dry for the same reason.
Bring the eggs to room temperature.

steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp of the oil in a wide kadhai and fry the okra over high heat, undisturbed for the first 3 minutes so it sears rather than steams.
steps.tip: Do not stir constantly and do not cover the pan. Both make it slimy.

steps.text: Keep frying 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until the pieces are browned at the edges and no longer sticky. Lift them out onto a plate.
Add the last tbsp of oil and fry the onion until golden, 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and green chilli and fry 1 minute.
Stir in turmeric, chilli powder, cumin and coriander powder for 30 seconds.
Return the okra with salt, toss 2 minutes to coat, then spread it into an even layer.
Make four hollows and crack in the eggs. Season with salt and black pepper.
Cover and cook on low 7-9 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still run.
steps.tip: If your lid does not fit well, add a tablespoon of water at the pan edge to raise steam.

steps.text: Squeeze over the lemon, scatter the coriander leaves and serve hot with rotli.

storage: Eat the same day. The okra will not stay crisp; leftovers keep 1 day refrigerated and are best reheated uncovered in a hot pan.
